expectations.text: Cites the EDPB's FINAL Guidelines on the DSA–GDPR interplay (Guidelines 3/2025, finalised September 2026)
expectations.evidence: Only "guidelines on the interplay under development" — the final Guidelines 3/2025 (finalised September 2026) are not cited.

expectations.text: States the core principle: cumulative, coherent application — DSA compliance does not displace GDPR duties
expectations.evidence: "designed to apply together... without prejudice to Union law on personal data protection"; "Do not treat DSA compliance as a lawful basis for broader data collection."

expectations.text: Gives concrete touchpoints: notice-and-action, recommender-system transparency/options, and the DSA advertising bans (profiling with special-category data; ads targeted at minors) all involve personal data and need a GDPR lawful basis
expectations.evidence: "Art. 26(3) bans ads based on profiling using special category data... Art. 28(2) bans profiling-based ads to... minors"; recommenders "Art. 38 requires... one option not based on profiling... personalisation based on profiling still needs a valid GDPR basis"; notice-and-action "You need a lawful basis (usually legal obligation under Art. 6(1)(c))".

expectations.text: Notes regulator coordination: Digital Services Coordinators/Commission and DPAs are steered toward consistent enforcement
expectations.evidence: "national Digital Services Coordinators and the Commission... data protection authorities... the EDPB and the Commission have said they will coordinate."

expectations.text: Gives practical advice: map each DSA-driven processing operation into the RoPA with its own basis and transparency
expectations.evidence: Recommends an "integrated compliance map: DSA article, data processed, GDPR basis, retention, and recipients" but never maps DSA processing into the RoPA (Art. 30 records) as the assertion requires.
